_notes: Example exec policy for arma_exec. Install: cp to ~/.config/armamentarium/exec.json, chmod 0644.
Keep it OUTSIDE every root an agent can write (the router refuses a policy that is group/world-writable or not yours).
Anything not matched by a rule is refused. Options not listed in a rule's 'options' are refused. argv never touches a shell.
mode: 'always' runs without approval; 'elevated' needs a live grant: arma-elevate exec <rule> [host] [ttl].
Placeholders: {int} {name} {word} {unit} {host} {time} {text} {ref} {dataset}; '?' suffix = optional; {path:ROOT} must resolve under a named root; {file:ROOT} is the same but never a directory.
A trailing '...' on the LAST positional ({file:ROOT...}) takes one or more values, each checked. git-add uses it: name every file; no -A, no '.', no directory.
git_identity: the author/committer stamped on every agent git command, so agent commits are distinguishable from yours in every repo.
Edit roots to match your machine. This example assumes code in ~/projects/<owner>/<repo>.

git-status.description: Working-tree status of any repo under ~/projects

git-diff.description: Changes, summary forms only (patch text could run textconv)

git-add.description: Stage named files only: one or more per call; never a directory, -A or '.'

git-push.description: Never --force. Needs a grant, so the operator always knows a push happened

journal.description: Read the journal (join the systemd-journal group to see system messages without sudo)

unit-restart.description: Needs a grant AND an exact NOPASSWD sudoers line for this command
